contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: after overwrite the point payload equals the provided payload; previously stored keys absent from the new payload are removed
contract_grounding.note: Per the violates-declaration self-check: the quoted assertion is read literally — observed readback {"new": 2} DOES equal the provided payload and the previously stored keys (keep, nested) absent from it were removed, so the un-keyed end-state promise was kept, and the observed parameter (key) is OUTSIDE this quote's constraint domain (the assertion is silent about key; no constraint in structured_contract.json covers the key parameter — the violated promise lives one layer up in the endpoint page's request-schema field key='Assigns payload to each point that satisfy this path of property', for which the contract has no dedicated constraint); the script used the cited constraint + [SPEC] key semantics as a composite oracle, so whether the observed whole-payload over-reach (sibling 'keep' destroyed despite documented path-scoped assignment) counts as violating this state constraint vs a schema-publication defect is the auditor's adjudication.

mundane_explanation.surviving: Doc-vs-impl divergence on the overwrite face: the published SetPayload schema (shared by the POST set-payload and PUT overwrite-payload endpoints) advertises key as a path-scoped assignment selector on the PUT page, while both overwrite handlers (REST do_overwrite_payload and gRPC overwrite_payload) explicitly discard it per in-source by-design comments, silently accepting the field with 200 and destroying sibling top-level keys for any client trusting the schema; whether this is a specification defect (schema should not publish key on the PUT face, or the face should 4xx on it) rather than an implementation defect is left to the chain-auditor.
